files_changed.summary: added SupabaseURL, DatabaseURL, MembershipCacheTTL, DB pool bound fields
pgxpool.NewWithConfig per §7.9 (Exec mode, StatementCacheCapacity=0, sizing from config); removed postgres/doc.go
Verifier: fetch/cache Supabase JWKS, verify RS256/ES256, issuer + expiry checks, returns AuthUserID
Authorizer: ResolveProfileID, IsTeamMember, IsTeamLeader, CanAccessSession, exact SQL mirror
generic ttlCache[K] + CachedAuthorizer wrapping the three membership checks, 60s default
Auth(): Bearer token -> Verify -> ResolveProfileID -> gin context
GET /v1/me — proves the chain end to end
NewRouter(cfg, db) wires Auth() over a /v1 group with /v1/me
constructs the pgx pool via postgres.NewPool, passes to NewRouter, closes on shutdown
re-added errs.New(status, message), needed by jwt.go/authorizer.go (this is new for this task, not a leftover from the rolled-back task 002)
added github.com/jackc/pgx/v5, github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 via go get + go mod tidy

decisions: Chose JWKS/RS256+ES256 verification per §5.6's literal wording ('verify via JWKS'), not Supabase's legacy HS256 shared-secret mode — flagged as a real risk in analyze.json if the live project actually uses the legacy mode.

DB interface in authorizer.go is the narrow QueryRow-only shape (satisfied structurally by *pgxpool.Pool) rather than a full repository interface, so tests use a 20-line fake instead of a mock framework or testcontainers.

Generics (ttlCache[K]) used for the three membership caches instead of three near-duplicate hand-written maps — same amount of code as one, avoids copy-paste drift between member/leader/session cache logic.

No cache invalidation-on-role-change hook implemented (§5.6 mentions it) — TTL-only, since no pub/sub or DB trigger wiring exists anywhere in this codebase yet; noted in analyze.json as an accepted 60s-late-worst-case gap.
commands_run: go run ./cmd/gateway + curl /healthz (200), /v1/me no token (401 missing bearer token), /v1/me garbage token (401 invalid token) — pool construction succeeded without a live Postgres connection (pgxpool connects lazily)
